sections.title: Processor
sections.name: Intel Core i5-4590
sections.note: A 2014 design with four cores and no Hyper-Threading, so four threads in total. It has an integrated GPU that this server does not use.
rows: DDR3-1600, two channels, 32 GB at most, no ECC
Q2 2014. Intel discontinued it in July 2017

sections.title: Motherboard
sections.name: MSI B85M-E45
sections.note: A micro-ATX board on the Intel B85 chipset. It sets the limits for everything else here: 32 GB of DDR3 and one graphics slot.

sections.title: Memory
sections.name: 24 GB Goodram DDR3-1600
sections.note: Upgraded in October 2026. The two pairs of modules differ, so the last 8 GB runs on one channel only and has less bandwidth.
rows: 2 × 8 GB dual-rank in channel A, 2 × 4 GB single-rank in channel B
Up to 25.6 GB/s across both channels
8 GB below the board's 32 GB limit
sections.slotsCaption: Each cell is 1 GB. All four slots are full.

sections.title: Graphics
sections.name: Radeon R7 250, 2 GB
sections.note: A low-end card from Gigabyte (GV-R725OC-2GI, revision 3.0). Its memory is DDR3, not GDDR5. The monitor connects to it.
rows: AMD Cape Verde, 28 nm, 512 stream processors

sections.title: Storage
sections.name: 876 GB across three drives
sections.note: Two SSDs and one laptop hard disk, all on SATA. The hard disk's link runs at 3 Gb/s because that is the drive's own limit.
rows: 120 GB SSD, SATA III, 2.5 inch. Boot drive
500 GB hard disk, 5400 rpm, 8 MB cache, SATA II, 2.5 inch
sections.drivesCaption: Each cell is about 10 GB of raw capacity.

sections.title: Power supply
sections.name: 300 W Power Man
sections.note: An In Win unit rated 80 PLUS Bronze. The graphics card draws from the slot only, so it needs no extra power lead.

sections.title: Case
sections.name: Compact micro-ATX tower
sections.note: The case that came with the build. I haven't measured the clearance for longer cards.

sources: Read from the machine on 10 Oct 2026, and checked against the Intel, MSI and Gigabyte specification pages.
